critical.text: Are appropriate public protection procedures in place for an incident, covering evacuation, invacuation, lockdown and communication?
critical.why: Section 5 requires appropriate, reasonably practicable public protection procedures. Standard-tier premises are not expressly required to document them under section 7; enhanced-tier premises and qualifying events have additional documentation duties.
critical.actionNo: Establish proportionate procedures for evacuation, invacuation, lockdown and communication; make sure staff who carry them out understand their roles. Document the arrangements as appropriate to the duty tier.

critical.findingNo: Appropriate public protection procedures are not clearly in place across the four statutory procedure areas.
critical.findingPartly: Some public protection procedures exist, but coverage or practical implementation is incomplete or uncertain.
critical.findingYes: Public protection procedures for evacuation, invacuation, lockdown and communication appear to be in place, subject to site-specific review.
critical.notes: Critical statutory-aligned safeguard. Lack of a written procedures document alone is not proof of a standard-tier breach.

critical.text: If a threat was nearby, could the site be secured quickly (lockdown)?
critical.why: Lockdown protects occupants from external threats.
critical.actionNo: Create a lockdown procedure with defined actions.
critical.actionPartly: Improve speed and consistency of implementation.
critical.findingNo: The site does not appear able to lock down quickly during a nearby threat.
critical.findingPartly: Some lockdown capability exists, but it may not yet be fast or consistent enough.
critical.findingYes: The site appears capable of securing quickly during a nearby threat.

criticalPartly.text: When evacuation is the safer response to a threat, can staff promptly guide people away from danger using appropriate routes?
criticalPartly.why: The appropriate response depends on the threat and its location. Evacuation may be needed, but invacuation or lockdown may be safer in other circumstances.
criticalPartly.actionNo: Develop an evacuation procedure that enables staff to move people safely away from danger when evacuation is appropriate; consider alternative responses when leaving would increase risk.
criticalPartly.actionPartly: Clarify when evacuation is appropriate, how safe routes are selected and how staff will guide people without placing them in greater danger.
criticalPartly.actionYes: Keep safe evacuation arrangements under review and practise decision-making with the relevant staff; avoid assuming that evacuation is always the correct response.
criticalPartly.findingNo: There is no dependable way to carry out a safe, timely evacuation when the circumstances call for it.
criticalPartly.findingPartly: Evacuation arrangements exist, but decisions, safe routes or prompt implementation need improvement.
criticalPartly.findingYes: Staff appear able to implement evacuation promptly when it is the safer protective response.
criticalPartly.notes: Critical procedure check: does not imply automatic or simultaneous evacuation in every terrorist incident.

criticalPartly.text: During an incident, could you stop people entering or leaving the site if required?
criticalPartly.why: Uncontrolled movement increases exposure and confusion.

q.notes: Supporting good practice, not a universal statutory named-person register or tracking requirement.

q.text: Are staff expected to challenge or report unknown or unauthorised individuals on site?
q.why: Unchallenged individuals increase vulnerability.
q.findingNo: Staff are not clearly expected to challenge or report unknown individuals on site.
q.findingPartly: The expectation exists informally, but it is not yet applied consistently.
q.findingYes: Staff appear clearly expected to challenge or report unknown individuals.

q.text: Is access to the site controlled so unauthorised people cannot enter freely?
q.why: Uncontrolled access increases vulnerability.
q.findingNo: Site access is not sufficiently controlled against unauthorised entry.
q.findingPartly: Some access controls exist, but they are not yet consistent across the site.
q.findingYes: Site access appears to be controlled against unauthorised entry.
q.notes: Enhanced duty relevance; hide or soften for standard if needed.

q.text: Are visitors signed in and appropriately supervised while on site?
q.why: Unsupervised visitors create risk.
q.findingNo: Visitors are not being signed in and supervised in a reliable way.
q.findingPartly: Visitor controls exist, but supervision or consistency needs improvement.
q.findingYes: Visitors appear to be signed in and supervised appropriately.

q.text: Can you manage movement safely during busy times (e.g. start/end of day, events)?
q.why: Crowding and unmanaged movement increase risk.
q.findingNo: Movement is not managed safely enough during busy periods.
q.findingPartly: Some movement management exists, but busy periods are not yet handled consistently.
q.findingYes: Movement appears manageable during busy periods.

q.text: Are there physical measures (e.g. locked doors, gates, barriers) that make it harder to access the site?
q.why: Physical measures reduce vulnerability.
q.findingNo: Physical measures to reduce access vulnerability are not clearly in place.
q.findingPartly: Some physical measures exist, but coverage or robustness needs improvement.
q.findingYes: Physical measures appear to be in place to make access more difficult.

q.text: Have you identified and recorded weak points where someone could access or exploit the site?
q.why: Unidentified vulnerabilities remain exploitable.
q.actionNo: Conduct site assessment and identify weak points.
q.findingNo: Weak points have not been clearly identified and recorded.
q.findingPartly: Some vulnerabilities are known, but recording or follow-up is incomplete.
q.findingYes: Weak points appear to have been identified and recorded.

q.text: Do staff have a simple and quick way to report suspicious activity?
q.why: Fast reporting enables timely action.
q.findingNo: Staff do not have a simple and quick reporting route for suspicious activity.
q.findingPartly: A reporting route exists, but it is not yet simple or quick enough.
q.findingYes: A simple reporting route appears to be available to staff.

q.text: Are reported concerns reviewed and acted on promptly?
q.why: Delayed response increases risk.
q.findingNo: Reported concerns are not clearly being reviewed and acted on promptly.
q.findingPartly: Concerns are reviewed to some extent, but timeliness or ownership needs improvement.
q.findingYes: Reported concerns appear to be reviewed and acted on promptly.

q.text: Can authorised staff send instructions or alerts during an incident?
q.why: Coordinated response requires authorised communication.
q.findingNo: Authorised staff cannot clearly send instructions or alerts during an incident.
q.findingPartly: Some alerting capability exists, but permissions, reach, or clarity need improvement.
q.findingYes: Authorised staff appear able to send instructions or alerts during an incident.

q.text: Are incidents or near misses recorded and reviewed?
q.why: Recording enables learning and improvement.
q.findingNo: Incidents and near misses are not being recorded and reviewed in a structured way.
q.findingPartly: Recording happens in part, but the review process needs improvement.
q.findingYes: Incidents and near misses appear to be recorded and reviewed.

q.text: Is it clear who can escalate a concern into a wider response (e.g. lockdown, evacuation)?
q.why: Unclear escalation delays action.
q.findingNo: It is not clear who can escalate a concern into wider protective action.
q.findingPartly: Escalation exists in part, but the chain of authority is not yet clear enough.
q.findingYes: The escalation route appears clear for wider response actions.
q.notes: Important bridge between reporting and response.

q.text: Are your emergency procedures written, accessible, and able to be provided if required?
q.why: Documentation supports compliance and audit.
q.findingNo: Emergency procedures are not clearly written, accessible, and ready to be provided if required.
q.findingPartly: Procedures exist, but accessibility, completeness, or readiness for review needs improvement.
q.findingYes: Emergency procedures appear written, accessible, and ready to be provided if required.

q.text: Have you checked whether your procedures would work in practice (e.g. through drills or structured review)?
q.why: Untested procedures may fail during real incidents.
q.actionNo: Carry out practical reviews or drills.
q.findingNo: Procedures have not been sufficiently checked in practice.
q.findingPartly: Some practical checking has happened, but depth or consistency needs improvement.
q.findingYes: Procedures appear to have been checked in practice.

q.text: Do you keep records of training, drills, reviews, and key decisions?
q.why: Records provide evidence of compliance and improvement.
q.findingNo: Records of training, drills, reviews, and decisions are not being maintained adequately.
q.findingPartly: Some records exist, but completeness or organisation needs improvement.
q.findingYes: Relevant records appear to be maintained.

q.text: Do you review and update your procedures regularly and when changes occur?
q.why: Outdated procedures reduce effectiveness.
q.findingNo: Procedures are not being reviewed and updated regularly enough.
q.findingPartly: Reviews happen in part, but not yet consistently or when changes occur.
q.findingYes: Procedures appear to be reviewed and updated appropriately.

q.text: Is there a clearly named person responsible for security and preparedness?
q.why: Clear accountability is essential.
q.findingNo: There is no clearly named person responsible for security and preparedness.
q.findingPartly: A responsible lead may exist, but accountability is not yet fully clear.
q.findingYes: A clearly named responsible person appears to be in place.

q.text: Do staff understand their role during an incident?
q.why: Role clarity improves response effectiveness.
q.findingNo: Staff do not appear to understand their role during an incident clearly enough.
q.findingPartly: Role understanding exists in part, but it is not yet consistent across staff.
q.findingYes: Staff appear to understand their role during an incident.

q.text: Do you coordinate with external partners where needed (e.g. police, local authority)?
q.why: Coordination supports effective response.
q.findingNo: Relevant external coordination is not yet clearly in place where needed.
q.findingPartly: Some external coordination exists, but it needs to be stronger or clearer.
q.findingYes: External coordination appears to be in place where needed.

q.text: Do you apply the same safety procedures during events or out-of-hours use?
q.why: Events can increase risk exposure.
q.findingNo: Normal safety procedures are not clearly being applied to events or out-of-hours use.
q.findingPartly: Some procedures carry over, but event and out-of-hours use is not yet covered consistently.
q.findingYes: Safety procedures appear to apply during events and out-of-hours use.

q.text: Are roles and responsibilities clearly defined for events?
q.why: Events require clear leadership and roles.
q.findingNo: Event roles and responsibilities are not clearly defined.
q.findingPartly: Some event roles are known, but clarity or briefing needs improvement.
q.findingYes: Event roles and responsibilities appear clearly defined.

q.text: Is access controlled during events?
q.why: Uncontrolled access increases risk.
q.findingNo: Event access is not sufficiently controlled.
q.findingPartly: Some event access controls exist, but they are not yet consistent or reliable.
q.findingYes: Event access appears to be controlled.

q.text: Do you assess each event to ensure appropriate safety procedures are in place?
q.why: Each event may present different risks and requirements.
q.findingNo: Individual events are not being assessed to confirm that appropriate safety procedures are in place.
q.findingPartly: Some event assessment happens, but it is not yet consistent or detailed enough.
q.findingYes: Events appear to be assessed individually for appropriate safety procedures.
q.notes: Good event-specific control and report item.

actions.question: Are appropriate public protection procedures in place for an incident, covering evacuation, invacuation, lockdown and communication?
actions.recommendation: Establish proportionate procedures for evacuation, invacuation, lockdown and communication; make sure staff who carry them out understand their roles. Document the arrangements as appropriate to the duty tier.
actions.note: SYNTHETIC: action completed and checked at November reassessment.

actions.question: If a threat was nearby, could the site be secured quickly (lockdown)?
actions.recommendation: Create a lockdown procedure with defined actions.
actions.note: SYNTHETIC: action completed and checked at November reassessment.

actions.question: When evacuation is the safer response to a threat, can staff promptly guide people away from danger using appropriate routes?
actions.recommendation: Clarify when evacuation is appropriate, how safe routes are selected and how staff will guide people without placing them in greater danger.

actions.note: SYNTHETIC: action completed and checked at November reassessment.
